---
title: "Acceptance and Handoff"
execute:
  eval: false
---

This checklist is the production-readiness record. Record date, operator,
application revision, release ID, evidence location, and result for every item.
A repository build can be complete while VM-side acceptance remains pending.

## External readiness gates

All four items must be resolved before declaring production ready.

| Gate | Required evidence | Owner/result |
|---|---|---|
| Matching TLS private key | Exact key path, certificate serial/SAN/expiry, matching public-key hashes, successful chain validation | |
| Service sender authorization | Written relay authorization for `ppsv-service@biochem.mpg.de` under the configured SMTP account | |
| Real ticket requester/auto-reply test | Ticket ID, headers, requester address, chosen mode, and proof of exactly one acknowledgement | |
| External backup and pool policy | External mount identity, retention, alerting, successful restore drill, and approved pool snapshot/restore procedure | |

An unresolved row is a release blocker. Do not replace missing evidence with an
assumption or a successful local unit test.

## Automated repository checks

From a clean checkout with locked dependencies restored:

```bash
Rscript -e 'renv::restore(project = "ppsvf-app", prompt = FALSE)'
Rscript tests/testthat.R
bash -n scripts/*.sh deploy.sh
```

Record the complete output. The suite must cover fresh schema/seeds, the exact
roles/modules/statuses, shared request IDs, the 18+8 field contract, inquiry
branch, Unicode/multiline edits, archive behavior, PDF content, direct backend
authorization, mail branches/retries, and unsafe storage cases. A failed or
skipped security-critical test is not accepted without a reviewed issue and
explicit risk decision.

## Deployment verifier

Create a short-lived mode-`0600` netrc for a dedicated LDAP test account. This
allows the verifier to use normal CA validation while proving authenticated,
spoofed-header, and WebSocket behavior:

```text
machine ppcf-vm.biochem.mpg.de
login LDAP_TEST_USERNAME
password LDAP_TEST_PASSWORD
```

```bash
sudo chmod 600 /root/ppsv-test.netrc
sudo scripts/verify_deployment.sh \
  --netrc /root/ppsv-test.netrc \
  --role-user ORDINARY_LDAP_USERNAME \
  --role-technician grzejszc \
  --role-admin yeroslaviz
sudo shred -u /root/ppsv-test.netrc
```

Never add `-k` or `--insecure` to make a TLS check pass. Full verification also
fails until `PPSV_SERVICE_IDENTITY_AUTHORIZED_ACK`,
`PPSV_TICKET_E2E_TEST_ACK`, and `PPSV_POOL_SNAPSHOT_POLICY_ACK` are `1`; each
value must be changed only after its evidence is recorded. It verifies that the
live backup mount source exactly matches `PPSV_BACKUP_EXPECTED_SOURCE` and the
facility pool matches `PPSV_POOL_EXPECTED_SOURCE`.

## Network, TLS, and redirects

- [ ] `curl -I http://ppcf-vm.biochem.mpg.de/` redirects to canonical HTTPS.
- [ ] `curl -I https://ppcf-vm.biochem.mpg.de/` validates the CA/chain and
  redirects to `/ppsvf-app/`.
- [ ] The presented certificate SAN covers `ppcf-vm.biochem.mpg.de`, is not
  near expiry, and matches the installed private key.
- [ ] An unauthenticated `/ppsvf-app/` request receives the expected LDAP
  challenge.
- [ ] `ss -ltnp` shows port 3838 only on `127.0.0.1` (or loopback equivalent),
  never `0.0.0.0`, `[::]`, or an external address.
- [ ] Apache proxies both HTTP and WebSocket traffic only to loopback.
- [ ] In an authenticated browser, DevTools shows the Shiny WebSocket upgrade
  succeeding and the live session continues after reactive input changes.
- [ ] HSTS, `nosniff`, and same-origin referrer headers are present on HTTPS.

## LDAP and spoof resistance

- [ ] A normal LDAP user can sign in and sees the expected normalized username,
  name, email, group, and phone values.
- [ ] Verified LDAP name/email are read-only; missing values are editable and
  visibly marked unverified.
- [ ] A forged unauthenticated `X-Remote-User: forged-admin` header does not
  bypass LDAP.
- [ ] The same header on an authenticated request is replaced by the real LDAP
  identity.
- [ ] A query parameter or cookie cannot choose or replace identity.
- [ ] Production environment contains `AUTH_MODE=ldap`; there is no local
  password or default credential.
- [ ] Deactivating a non-admin account blocks it; reactivation restores only
  its allowlist-derived role.
- [ ] `b_profa` membership alone grants no application privilege.

## Three-role authorization exercise

Use one ordinary LDAP account, one allowlisted technician, and one allowlisted
administrator.

### User

- [ ] Can submit a service request and a general inquiry.
- [ ] Can view/edit only their own non-closed request and add an input file.
- [ ] Can still view but cannot edit a `Closed` own request.
- [ ] Cannot access another owner's direct request ID, file, or PDF.
- [ ] Cannot change status/assignee, upload a result, archive, manage users, or
  retry mail, including through forged/direct Shiny events.

### Technician

- [ ] Can view/edit all requests, add inputs/results, select any of the seven
  statuses, add a history note, and assign a technician/admin.
- [ ] Cannot archive a request or file, manage users, or run admin mail retry.

### Admin

- [ ] Has staff functions plus soft archive for requests/files.
- [ ] Can view the user directory and activate/deactivate a non-admin account.
- [ ] Sees roles as derived/read-only.
- [ ] Can retry only a failed outbox item.
- [ ] Has no permanent purge operation.

## Form, lifecycle, and PDF exercise

- [ ] The request-type selector starts empty and contains eight ordered services
  plus `General inquiry / consultation`.
- [ ] Each service displays the seeded description and safe external HTTPS link.
- [ ] A service form shows exactly 18 required and eight optional workbook
  fields; positive-number and nullable Yes/No validation behave as documented.
- [ ] `Cleavage Size` and `Aliquot size` accept value+unit text; literal `N/A`
  works only for required textual fields.
- [ ] General inquiry hides protein and billing fields, requires contact,
  subject, and message, and stores an optional related service without adding a
  ninth module row.
- [ ] Concurrent test submissions use one gap-safe allocation mechanism and
  return unique sequential `PPSVnnnnnn` IDs across both request kinds.
- [ ] Unicode, multiline values, edits, assignment, and all seven status changes
  round-trip correctly; history records actor, UTC timestamp, and note.
- [ ] The PPSV PDF contains request/module, contact/scientific fields, current
  status/history, and file manifest, with no cost/invoice content.

## Mail exercise

- [ ] Request and outbox records commit together before SMTP is attempted.
- [ ] Chosen `PPSV_TICKET_MODE` has the evidence required by the decision test.
- [ ] Form email is absent from `From`, `Reply-To`, and acknowledgement recipient.
- [ ] Missing LDAP email uses the service sender without `Reply-To`, suppresses
  acknowledgement, and is visibly flagged.
- [ ] Fixed-sender failures remain durable and follow immediate, 5-minute,
  30-minute, 2-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour attempts.
- [ ] LDAP-`From` rejection activates the service fallback deterministically.
- [ ] Both-send failure is shown as failed; the UI never claims ticket success.
- [ ] The requester receives exactly one acknowledgement, and a ticket-link
  sentence appears only when a real ticket URL is returned.

## Storage and permissions exercise

Inspect ACLs and create a disposable service-user probe:

```bash
sudo getfacl /fs/pool/pool-ppsvf-projects
probe="/fs/pool/pool-ppsvf-projects/.ppsv-handoff-$$"
sudo -u ppsvf-shiny-user bash -c \
  'umask 0007; mkdir "$1"; chmod 2770 "$1"; touch "$1/probe"; chmod 0660 "$1/probe"' \
  bash "$probe"
sudo stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' "$probe" "$probe/probe"
sudo -u ppsvf-shiny-user unlink "$probe/probe"
sudo -u ppsvf-shiny-user rmdir "$probe"
```

- [ ] Service user writes primary pool and fallback; created directories/files
  are `2770`/`0660` with the expected ACL.
- [ ] A request appears at `PPSVnnnnnn/{inputs,results}` and the database keeps
  generated name, original name, size, uploader, location, and SHA-256.
- [ ] Traversal names, symlinks, and unauthorized direct IDs are rejected.
- [ ] Cumulative 75 MB limit is enforced.
- [ ] With the pool unavailable, a file goes to persistent fallback and the
  request is flagged; with both stores unavailable, file submission fails.
- [ ] Reconciliation verifies both checksums before changing the database and
  does not overwrite a mismatched destination.
- [ ] A technician cannot archive/delete a file; an admin archive is soft.

## Backup and restore exercise

- [ ] Nightly timer is enabled and a fresh database backup and fallback archive
  exist on the verified external mount with matching SHA-256 sidecars.
- [ ] Retention is 30 days and old-artifact removal has been observed safely.
- [ ] `restore_backup.sh` read-only validation succeeds.
- [ ] A full restore has succeeded on a disposable environment and the evidence
  includes record/file/PDF/download checks.
- [ ] Facility pool snapshot and single-request/full-pool restore procedures are
  approved and tested.
- [ ] Operators understand that code rollback does not roll back migrations or
  data, and database restore can discard newer requests.

## Sign-off

Production readiness may be declared only when the four external gates and all
applicable checklist items have evidence. Record any deferred non-critical item
with owner, deadline, and accepted risk. Never describe repository delivery as
proof that TLS, SMTP, ticket, backup, or pool operations have passed on the VM.
